paper.title: Bandits with Probing: Optimal Regret and the Limits of Winner Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with probing, independent arms, MaxOnly feedback
unmapped: reward of an action is the maximum of the selected arms' rewards
comparator is the best fixed single arm, not the best k-set
arms are independent (product law across arms)
K = n arms, m = k probes, 2 <= k < n
settings.definition_quote: a learner selects at most $k$ of $n$ arms in each round, earns the largest of their rewards, and competes with the best fixed single arm. ... \MO reports only $W_t$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with probing, independent arms, AllProbe feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: reward of an action is the maximum of the selected arms' rewards
comparator is the best fixed single arm
arms are independent (product law)
settings.definition_quote: For a feedback channel $\Fbk$, the minimax value $\cV_{n,T}^{\Fbk,(k)}=\inf_{\pi_T}\sup_D R_T^{\pi_T}(D)$ takes the supremum over product laws $D=\bigotimes_iD_i$, that is, over independent arms; the superscripts $\mathrm{joint}$ and $\mathrm{seq}$ replace product laws by arbitrary joint i.i.d.\ laws and by fixed arrays, respectively. Policies may know $T$ and the channel.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with probing on fixed reward arrays, Contrast feedback
unmapped: Contrast feedback: action is a block or ordered pair of disjoint blocks; learner earns the max over the union but observes only the signed contrast of block maxima
reward of an action is the maximum of selected rewards; comparator is best fixed single arm
settings.definition_quote: Under \CT, an action is either one nonempty block or an ordered pair $(A,B)$ of disjoint nonempty blocks ... observes only the signed contrast $D_t=\max_{i\in B}X_{i,t}-\max_{i\in A}X_{i,t}$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with probing on fixed reward arrays, AllProbe feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: reward of an action is the maximum of selected rewards; comparator is best fixed single arm
settings.definition_quote: In the sequence model, a reward array $x\in[0,1]^{n\times T}$ is fixed before the policy's randomization.

settings.name_in_paper: Common-core virtual arms with pair probes, MaxOnly feedback
unmapped: virtual arm rewards X_i = max{Z_0, Z_i} with independent Z_0 (shared core) and Z_i; arms correlated through the core
regret measured against base benchmark b = max_i E Z_i
settings.definition_quote: Let $Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\in[0,1]$ be independent, drawn afresh in each round, and let $X_i=\max\{Z_0,Z_i\}$ ... We measure regret against the \emph{base} benchmark $b$

settings.name_in_paper: Two-probe contrast policy on fixed arrays
unmapped: Contrast feedback: only the signed difference of the two probed rewards is observed; payoff is the max of the pair
comparator is best fixed single arm
settings.definition_quote: Consider first $m\ge2$ arms with losses $\ell_{i,t}=1-x_{i,t}$. In each round, the policy probes an anchor $A_t$ and an exploratory arm $B_t$ and incurs the loss $\min\{\ell_{A_t,t},\ell_{B_t,t}\}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Intermittent maximum-only observations M_rho, independent arms
unmapped: the maximum W_t is revealed only when an i.i.d. Bernoulli(rho) coin equals 1 (random erasures); rho unknown to the learner
payoff is the max of the selected arms; comparator best single arm; independent arms
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathsf M_\rho$ reveal a coin $C_t\sim\Bern(\rho)$ and, only when $C_t=1$, the maximum $W_t$, with no winning label

settings.name_in_paper: Intermittent maximum-only observations M_rho, independent arms (lower bound)
unmapped: maximum revealed only on Bernoulli(rho) coins; the learner may know rho and the channel

settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathsf M_\rho$ reveal a coin $C_t\sim\Bern(\rho)$ and, only when $C_t=1$, the maximum $W_t$, with no winning label

settings.name_in_paper: Winner feedback with intermittent Bernoulli-rounded values Bit_rho, fixed arrays
unmapped: winner label J_t always observed; value revealed only on Bernoulli(rho) coin, and replaced by a Bernoulli(W_t) bit; rho unknown
payoff max of selected arms; comparator best single arm
settings.definition_quote: the channel $\Fbk_\rho$ always reports the winner $J_t$ and a revelation coin $C_t\sim\Bern(\rho)$, and it reports $W_t$ when $C_t=1$. The channel $\Bit_\rho$ replaces each revealed value by a bit $Y_t$ with $Y_t\mid W_t\sim\Bern(W_t)$.

algorithms.name: MaxOnly policy (Algorithm 1: surplus-funded capital, five-round packets) with permanent random core
Two-probe contrast policy (centered estimator, mixed sampler, 1/2-Tsallis mirror descent) with grouping / contrast gate

conditions: 2 <= k < n (m = k probes, K = n arms)
independent arms (holds whenever every set of at most k arms has product law)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For independent arms in the stochastic model, \tfrac12\Phi_{n,k}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\AP,(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\BP,(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\MO,(k)}<46000\Phi_{n,k}(T). ... Each upper bound is attained by an explicit anytime policy.

results.notes: Phi_{n,k}(T) = ((n-k)/n) min{T, n/k}; K=n, m=k. Regret T mu* - E sum W_t.

conditions: hard instance: one deterministic reward-one arm at a uniformly random label, all others zero

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: \tfrac12\Phi_{n,k}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\AP,(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\BP,(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\MO,(k)}

results.notes: Holds even under AllProbe (all selected rewards observed), hence for BestProbe and MaxOnly too.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For arbitrary fixed arrays, \tfrac12\Phi_{n,k}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\AP,\mathrm{seq},(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\CT,\mathrm{seq},(k)}\le256\Phi_{n,k}(T).

results.notes: Also applies to joint i.i.d. rewards. AllProbe simulates Contrast, so the same upper bound holds under AllProbe.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For arbitrary fixed arrays, \tfrac12\Phi_{n,k}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\AP,\mathrm{seq},(k)}

results.notes: Hidden deterministic arm construction.

conditions: m >= 3 virtual arms (K denotes the paper's m here)
common-core model X_i = max{Z_0, Z_i} with independent Z's

source.label: thm:pair
source.quote: For \eqref{eq:core_model} with $m\ge3$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:pair} uses only numerical maxima and satisfies, at every deterministic physical horizon $T$, R_T(b):=Tb-\E\sum_{t\le T}W_t \le\frac{25307}{5}m-\frac{3471}{2}<5062m. The policy is anytime and uses no distributional parameters.

results.notes: Regret against base benchmark b = max_i E Z_i (not the best virtual arm); comparator set to not_applicable. Zero core recovers independent arms with pair probes, bounded regret O(m).

source.label: thm:ap_pair
source.quote: For every fixed array and horizon, the policy \eqref{eq:ap_sampler}--\eqref{eq:ap_update} satisfies \mbox{$R_T^{\mathrm{seq}}\le32(m-\sqrt m)$}.

results.notes: Learning rate does not depend on T, so anytime.

source.label: cor:maxonly_erasure
source.quote: For product rewards and $0<\rho\le1$, \tfrac18\Phi_{n,k,\rho}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\mathsf M_\rho,(k)}\le46000\Phi_{n,k,\rho}(T). One anytime policy attains the upper bound without knowing $\rho$. At $\rho=0$, the minimax value is exactly $\delta T$.

results.notes: Policy does not know rho. At rho=0 the value is exactly delta*T (attained by uniform random k-sets).

source.label: cor:maxonly_erasure
source.quote: For product rewards and $0<\rho\le1$, \tfrac18\Phi_{n,k,\rho}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\mathsf M_\rho,(k)}

results.notes: At rho=0 the minimax value is exactly delta*T.

bound.regime: rho in [0,1]; sqrt term infinite at rho=0

tuning: switch from label policy to numerical learner after the nk-th revelation

source.label: thm:dependence
source.quote: For every $\rho\in[0,1]$ and $\mathsf M\in\{\mathrm{joint},\mathrm{seq}\}$, \frac1{72}\mathcal R_{n,k,\rho}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\Fbk_\rho,\mathsf M,(k)}\le\cV_{n,T}^{\Bit_\rho,\mathsf M,(k)}\le44\mathcal R_{n,k,\rho}(T). One explicit anytime policy attains both upper bounds without knowing $\rho$.

results.notes: Stated for fixed arrays and joint i.i.d. rewards; recorded on fixed arrays (implies joint i.i.d.). Also holds for F_rho, which simulates Bit_rho. At rho=0 gives label-only law delta*min{T,(n+T)/k}.

bound.regime: rho in [0,1]; sqrt term infinite at rho=0

conditions: correlated joint i.i.d. hard family (uninformative winner labels)

source.label: thm:dependence
source.quote: For every $\rho\in[0,1]$ and $\mathsf M\in\{\mathrm{joint},\mathrm{seq}\}$, \frac1{72}\mathcal R_{n,k,\rho}(T)\le\cV_{n,T}^{\Fbk_\rho,\mathsf M,(k)}

results.notes: Also stated for fixed arrays (seq), which follows from the joint i.i.d. case. Lower bound applies to F_rho and hence to the weaker Bit_rho.

tuning: switch after the n-th numerical revelation

source.label: thm:numerical
source.quote: For every $n>k\ge2$, $T\ge1$, and $\rho\in[0,1]$, ... \le V^{\mathrm{val}}_{n,k,\rho}(T)\le46032U_{n,k,\rho}(T). One anytime policy, knowing neither $T$ nor $\rho$, attains the upper bound.

results.notes: U = delta*min{T,(n+T)/k, n/(k rho)}.

symbols.h: h = 1 if k <= n/2, h = log(e/delta) if k > n/2

source.label: thm:numerical
source.quote: \frac1{65536}\max\left\{\Phi_{n,k}(T),\delta\min\left\{\frac{T}{hk\ell_n(T)},\frac{n}{k\rho}\right\}\right\}\le V^{\mathrm{val}}_{n,k,\rho}(T)

results.notes: ell_n(T) = min{k, log(e+T/n)}.

source.label: thm:numerical
source.quote: For labels alone, the lower bound sharpens to V^{\mathrm{lab}}_{n,k}(T)\ge\frac1{4096}\max\left\{\Phi_{n,k}(T),\frac{\delta T}{k\ell_d(T)}\right\}.

results.notes: ell_d(T) = min{k, log(e+T/d)}, d = n-k.

source.label: cor:uniform_product
source.quote: For $\rho>0$, \inf_{\pi\ \mathrm{anytime}}\sup_{T\ge1}\sup_{D\ \mathrm{product}}R_T^\pi(D)\asymp\frac{n-k}{k\rho}, with universal constants.

results.notes: Upper side from the held MaxOnly policy (46000 delta n/(k rho)), which ignores labels.

symbols.h: h = 1 if k <= n/2, else log(e/delta)

source.label: cor:uniform_product
source.quote: Moreover, the finite-time value has this order whenever T\ge\frac{8hn}{\rho}\min\{k,\log(e+h/\rho)\}.

results.notes: Finite-time lower bound in the saturation regime; also gives the horizon-uniform lower bound for anytime policies.

symbols.C_slope: assumed slope constant C in R_T <= S + C delta T/k^2

conditions: policies satisfying R_T <= S(n,k) + C delta T / k^2 on every product instance

source.label: cor:exponential_startup
source.quote: Suppose label-only policies satisfy $R_T\le S(n,k)+C\delta T/k^2$ on every product instance, for one fixed finite $C>0$. Then some $c_C,\alpha_C>0$ satisfy S(2k,k)\ge c_C e^{\alpha_C k}/k for all sufficiently large $k$, even when the policies know the horizon.

results.notes: Lower bound on the startup term S of any regret bound with k^{-2} slope; quantity other.

source.label: prop:bit_separation
source.quote: For $n=3$, $k=2$, and $\rho\in[0,1]$, \frac1{400}\min\{T,\sqrt{T/\rho}\}\le\cV_{3,T}^{\Bit_\rho,(2)}\le18\min\{T,\sqrt{T/\rho}\}.

results.notes: Upper bound from Theorem thm:dependence specialised to n=3, k=2. At rho=1 the (J,Y) rate is Theta(sqrt T).

source.label: prop:bit_separation
source.quote: \frac1{400}\min\{T,\sqrt{T/\rho}\}\le\cV_{3,T}^{\Bit_\rho,(2)} ... At full revelation, feedback $(J,W)$, feedback $(J,Y)$ with $Y\mid W\sim\Bern(W)$, and feedback $J$ alone have product-law minimax rates $\Theta(1)$, $\Theta(\sqrt T)$, and $\Theta(T)$

results.notes: At rho=0 (labels only) gives T/400, i.e. Theta(T) for label-only feedback; Theta(1) for exact values is from Theorem thm:main.

conditions: policies restricted to |S_t| = k each round

source.label: prop:full_budget
source.quote: Restrict label-only policies to $|S_t|=k$ in every round. Their product-law minimax value is $\Theta(\delta\min\{T,(n+T)/k\})$, with universal constants.

results.notes: Upper constant 16 from eq. bp_label_upper (holds on any fixed array).

conditions: policies restricted to |S_t| = k in every round

source.label: prop:full_budget
source.quote: Restrict label-only policies to $|S_t|=k$ in every round. Their product-law minimax value is $\Theta(\delta\min\{T,(n+T)/k\})$, with universal constants.

results.notes: Constant from proof.

source.label: prop:quotas
source.quote: For $\beta<1$, the minimax regret is $\Theta(\Phi_\beta(T))$, with universal constants independent of the number of classes, both for product rewards with \MO and for fixed arrays with \CT. Each upper bound is attained by an anytime policy. For $\beta=1$, the value is zero.

results.notes: Proof gives < 46000 Phi_beta(T).

source.label: prop:quotas
source.quote: For $\beta<1$, the minimax regret is $\Theta(\Phi_\beta(T))$ ... both for product rewards with \MO and for fixed arrays with \CT.

results.notes: Constants from proof: < 384(1-beta)/beta or 164(1-beta).

source.label: prop:quotas
source.quote: Place a deterministic hidden good arm in a class attaining $\beta$ and zeros elsewhere. The quota of this class gives the lower bound $\Phi_\beta(T)/2$ by \eqref{eq:det_coverage}, even under \AP.

results.notes: Lower bound holds for product laws and fixed arrays, even under AllProbe.
